content.text:
Tesla’s April 13–16 move looks like a **coherent upside episode concentrated on April 14–15**, not a selloff/reversal: TSLA rose +0.99% to $352.42 on April 13, +3.34% to $364.20 on April 14, then +7.62% to $391.95 on April 15 on 113.8 million shares, before a modest -0.78% pullback to $388.90 on April 16 [1]. That path matches the two positive rolling signals: the strongest move was the April 13–15 +11.22% run, while the April 14–16 +6.78% signal shows the move largely held despite the final-day fade [1].

The firm-specific catalyst mix was strongest. UBS upgraded Tesla on April 14 from Sell to Neutral, saying the post-pullback valuation created a more balanced risk/reward while still flagging weak EV demand, higher investment needs, and slow progress in robotaxi/Optimus [2]. The setup also came after Tesla’s April 2 delivery report, where Q1 production of 408,386 vehicles exceeded deliveries of 358,023, and ahead of Q1 earnings scheduled for April 22, making positioning and expectations important [3]. On April 15, coverage tied the intraday pop to Elon Musk highlighting an AI5 chip milestone, the UBS upgrade, and Tesla’s deeper push into custom silicon, FSD subscriptions, Grok in vehicles, and chip-factory plans [4]. However, the same coverage noted cautious Barclays and TD Cowen comments, delivery-miss concerns, and fears that the Terafab effort could materially raise capex [4]. Intel’s April 7 announcement that it had joined the Terafab project with Tesla, SpaceX and xAI added credibility to the AI/robotics narrative, but press coverage also stressed that no SEC filing or detailed legal framework had been disclosed, so this was still more sentiment catalyst than fully underwritten financial event [5].

Industry and market forces also mattered. The consumer-discretionary proxy XLY rose +0.91%, +2.21%, and +1.49% on April 13–15 before dipping -0.47% on April 16, consistent with a modest positive industry contribution rather than an auto-specific sector surge [6]. The macro tape was much more important: on April 15 the S&P 500 rose 0.8% to 7,022.95 and the Nasdaq gained 1.6%, with AP attributing the record close to hopes the economy could avoid a worst-case Iran-war scenario as ceasefire talks advanced [7]. Axios similarly described a record-setting rally driven by hopes the Iran war would fade, signs of resilient consumer spending, and hedge-fund/CTA buying after weeks of de-risking [8]. Overall, the web record supports the attribution: Tesla-specific AI/analyst-positioning news explains the dominant firm component, while a powerful growth-stock market rally explains the large SPY contribution; evidence for the small industry term is mostly price co-movement rather than a distinct discretionary-sector news catalyst.
